newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore stocks end firm, play on warrants.
newsitem.headline: Singapore stocks end firm, play on warrants.

text.p: Singapore stocks ended firm on Tuesday but a spate of profit-taking late in the afternoon on selected index stocks sent the Straits Times Industrials (STI) Index into negative territory, dealers said.
"The retail players took the opportunity to take profit (in key index stocks) but their volumes were thin," said a broker.
"Domestic liquidity is very good today because retail investors are also looking at IPO stocks apart from speculative Malaysian counters," said a dealer with a European institution.
The STI Index ended 6.34 points down, at 2,197.05 after trading to a high of 2,211.79.
Turnover was an active 323 million shares, with gainers leading losers by 357 to 65.
HK Land was active on talk that there was of a buyer for one of its properties. The stock chalked up volume of over 8.2 million shares. It ended at US$2.99, up three cents.

Retail interest in second liners like Labroy Marine led to active volume of 10 million shares. It ended at Singapore $1.82, up S$0.08. Jack Chia warrants surged 22 percent higher to S$0.72 and Eltech warrants up 20 percent by S$0.32.
